title: Putting the Unit Together: Concession, Contrast, Consequence

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: This lesson puts the unit's devices together. The reading text about Babits' 1928 essay *Az írástudók árulása* uses all of them: subordinate concessions (*jóllehet*), antithetical contrasts (*ezzel szemben*), parallel periodic balance (*nemcsak... hanem... is*), and resonant moral conclusions (*mindebből következően*).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: The text sets passing politics against the lasting standard of truth and human dignity (*az igazság és emberség örök mércéje*). An intellectual who trades universal values for partisan advantage commits what Julien Benda called *la trahison des clercs*, the treason of the intellectuals.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: Although the demands of the age are pressing... (concession)
...az írástudó mégsem szolgálhatja ki a mulandó hatalmat...
...the intellectual nevertheless cannot cater to transient power... (antithesis)
...consequently from all this, his responsibility is universal. (consequence)
